correctness.rationale: After translating projected apex to origin, a tilted unit normal u=re+sqrt(1−r²)n has exact width rb+max(ra,h sqrt(1−r²)), a=h_C(e), b=h_C(−e). With projection in base a,b>=0, branch switch r0=h/sqrt(h²+a²); initial concave branch has endpoint minimum and second branch is nondecreasing, yielding min{h,h(a+b)/sqrt(h²+a²)}; reversing e gives symmetric max-denominator condition. Projection outside base yields b<0 in a separating direction and w<h for small r. The Bakaev–Polyanskii uncovered-volume bound with w=h is matched by the base-adjacent plank via similarity volume factor (1−W/h)^d. This is a symbolic proof, not a finite sweep.
